memory_candidates.content: When a document maintains more than one enumeration of the same closed list (e.g. a Signal-A instance table in one section and a downstream deduplication 'identity key' enumeration in another), incrementally extending one enumeration across separate edit passes without grepping the whole document for sibling enumerations of the same set is a real and easy-to-miss consistency gap. A final top-to-bottom read-through phase, done AFTER all incremental edits and treated as a genuine re-read rather than a rubber stamp, is the right place to catch it -- in this task it caught exactly one such gap (a dedup-rule enumeration left at four items after the source table grew to five).

For a verification-and-gap-closure plan (deliverables already written and committed by an earlier research phase; the plan only records verification and plans the gap closures), re-independently reproducing every claimed jq/grep/sed evidence command at implementation time -- not trusting the planner's verification table at face value -- is cheap (each check is a single command) and catches citation drift between planning and implementation. In this task every row still held, but the same discipline is what the document itself argues for (citations must be re-verified, never trusted from a prior report) and applying it recursively to the plan's own verification table is consistent, not redundant.
